_note: TEACHES FIGHTING. Won by leaving the enemy nothing.
NO OBJECTIVES, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS FILE. `last_man_standing` is the
game's ordinary conquest rule, already built and already tested, so this scenario is
PLAYABLE BEFORE A LINE OF OBJECTIVE CODE EXISTS -- 15.1 + 15.3 + 15.5 and it runs.
That makes it the cheapest of the three and the one that proves the launch path on its
own, which is the opposite of how the plan read before 2026-09-01. The loader REFUSES
a last_man_standing scenario that carries objectives, because those rows would never
be read and silently ignoring an authored win condition loses the author's intent.
IT WAS SPECIFIED AS '0 ENEMY UNITS ON MAP' AND THAT IS NOT REACHABLE (owner's call,
2026-09-01). A Passive AI runs its whole economy and never attacks, so it keeps
training villagers from its town centre and the count refills faster than an early army
empties it -- the scenario would have been unwinnable while looking correct. Widening it
to units AND buildings is the conquest rule wearing the words a player reads as
'destroy the enemy', it needs no new rule, it keeps the Passive opponent, and it teaches
the lesson the scenario is named for: YOU CANNOT FINISH AN ENEMY BY CHASING THEIR
VILLAGERS. Take the town centre.
THE MAP TYPE MATTERS MORE HERE THAN IN THE OTHER TWO. A River map puts the two starts
on opposite banks, so finding the opponent is part of the lesson. Note that
_river_start_positions alternates banks by index, which splits an allied PAIR --
irrelevant at two players, and a real bug for a future 2v2 scenario.
name: How To Find Opponent and Attack
description: Somewhere across the river is another player. Build an army, go and find them, and leave them nothing.
message:
Train soldiers at the barracks, select them, and tap an enemy to attack. Use the minimap to find your opponent.

Goal: destroy every enemy unit AND building. Their villagers keep coming -- take their buildings.
